input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 (second instance) binds us, the Customer, not the Vendor: it prohibits developing, marketing, selling, or acquiring any competing product or service for the term plus twenty-four months in any territory. The scope is undefined ("any product or service that competes with Vendor") and the post-term tail exceeds 12 months, so it fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, which records that "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." We therefore flip the operator and drop the duration so the clause becomes an express permission, achieving the preferred position with no restriction on our business. (The separate no-hire covenant in the first Section 12.4 is addressed under its own rule.)

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.

proposal.summary: Convert Section 12.4 non-compete into an express permission, removing the restriction on Customer
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot restrict the products or businesses we may develop, sell, or acquire, so we have turned this covenant into an express permission, consistent with Section 12.3. If you need protection, we could discuss a restriction limited to one named competing product, during the term only and no longer than 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.
